newsitem.title: USA: Harnischfeger sees earnings possibly below outlook.
newsitem.headline: Harnischfeger sees earnings possibly below outlook.

text.p: Harnischfeger Industries Inc said Wednesday that earnings for its current fiscal year could be up to 10 percent below expectations due to second-half softness in its mining equipment business.
Shares in the heavy equipment manufacturer were off 1-7/8 to 41-1/8.
"We believe this is a short-term phenomenon," said chief executive Jeffery Grade.
Harnischfeger had been expected to earn $3.80 per share in its current fiscal year, according to the First Call consensus of 11 Wall Street analysts' forecasts.
The company said it had not anticipated the softness, but called it "remediable by year-end so as to have little or no impact on our 1998 performance."

"Harnischfeger's global mining businesses remain fundamentally very strong with our market share increasing and the profit enhancement produced by the Longwall International merger on track," Grade said.

The company said its mining equipment business, while still exhibiting strength globally and in the U.S. aftermarket, has had "a substantial mix change as well as anticipated weakness in the U.S. original equipment marketplace." The company said, "The net consequence of this softness could produce a reduction from year-end earnings expectations of up to 10 percent for the company."

Harnischfeger, a maker of equipment for mining, pulp and papermaking and material handling, on Wednesday reported net sales of $794.6 million in the second quarter ended April 30, up from $739.5 million in the same quarter last year.
Net income rose to $45 million from $33.6 million a year ago on the quarter.
Harnischfeger earned $2.88 per share before special items in its previous fiscal year ended October 31, 1996.
